"Something tells me that's not in the cards! ...Not this time, at least." *He looks back down to Cal.* "So how'z about this instead. You've put on a decent enough show that I'm in a good mood today. So, if you stand right there and can take one of my blows, I'll call it here on the festivities and... let the rest of your lot survive... But if you fall... A throaty chuckle then begins to bubble out and grow into a full blown belly laugh as the Ogre relaxes his stance and slams the butt of the spear into the deck of the ship.*

"Not bad! Not bad at all! HAHAHAH! I know you were something special!" *Bre'kahr admits.* "CREW! Grab our fallen! We're cutting this little dance short and shove'n off!!" *There are groans and grunts and yells of approval. But after another barked word from the captain, the pirates follow through on the command and warily make their way back to the ship.*

*A few mercernaries try their luck at getting revenge, only to be held back by their fellows, or overwhelmed by fortunately nonlethal throws and strikes from the pirates done in self-defense. The Captain is the last to the rails, but stopped for a moment to look back at Cal.* "What's your name, boy?" *He asks. But regardless of the answer, it gets another chuckle out of the captain before he hops off and begins making sail away from Cal's ship.*

*Once they are at some distance, Cal's captain gives the order to ready cannons, only to find that they had all been sabotaged during the chaos, requiring more time than they had for petty revenge before the other ships disappear into the night.*

But as your vision fades and pain turns to shock and ultimate numbness you See something else. Flashes, memories of what you once were. Running through a forest. Hair and claws and teeth and blood. You are being chased. The scene changes and you a figure set in sharp relief by torchlight. Its skin is the white of bone and its even whiter armor gleams with the radiance of the sun hidden by night. Even as you know you are dead there is still a guttural anger and hatred at this image, something that transcends even death. The image changes again and you see a bat. It flits and then is crushed. Another figure, this one small with white hands laughs a sickly sound. More hatred flares within you and it is like feeling dead muscle go taught and skin tear. Once again there is a shift and you see rumbling dirt and collapsing tunnels. Things fly in the sky, turning it black with feather and wing. The march of metal boots shakes the earth to its roots, burying everything. Shackles, sacks, bindings, the stink of unwashed bodies next to you that you just can't see. Then theres a whisper in the darkness, a guttural laughter you know well. Your master is there in these memories, even more bestial, much more solid, much greater. Rath manifests before you, his being burning a whole within your minds eye. Reality bending and shrinking away from his horrible majesty. You sense that some of this is out of place, and the words that dribble from his maw make it so.* "**You have perished supplicant, but there is still more to be done. Be reborn, and know that my will still needs adjudicating. Return to the maze and bring me my tribute.**" 
*Theres a sudden burning, a revelation as feeling returns you to flesh, of your sense reawakening and death being remade as life once more. Every facet of your being aches and cries out but you are alive once more, back within the haunted lands of the abyss, back under the shadow of Rath, even as he languishes on his ancient throne. There is more to be done.* Alright so I assume you head back to the maze? *the archway into the maze stands above you unchanged. Looking beyond the threshold you can tell that the passageways behind are different from the first time you entered. The maze never stays complacent.* *Its not hard to fall into a familiar pattern as you travel through the catacombs and hallways of the maze. Once again you parse out the path forward from clues of mathematics and riddle. Each answer is merely the guide to the next equation, the clues reifying themselves into course and path to travel. As you near a final piece you see a somewhat familiar growth upon the walls. Taking a closer look you realize this fungus is merely superficially similar to that of the alkilith. In fact as you continue along you notice as they warp and purify into seeming boils. They blister the walls along lines that give the vague image of claws trailing across the stone. As your clues converge into an answer you see the thing. A humanoid creature with a head in the mockery of a goat squats in a corner. It is riddled with diseased flesh, and its mane of hair is oily and thick. Theres a gurgling in the back of its throat as it acknowledges your presence before it leaps into the air with surprising agility, its barbed tail flicking out in attack*

input: *A brown wolf trots and searches for prey within the forests, and having no luck, decides to push closer to the river to catch one searching for a drink. Or perhaps to catch a fish, if it feels like it. As it grows closer, though, its ears pick up the melody from a flute on top of the river's churning. Growing interested, it moves slowly towards the source of the sound, taking care to move quietly to avoid attention. Its eyes peek through the trees to see who might have been strange enough to come so deep in the forests today.*
output: *Realizing that it had likely been noticed as the tune stops, the wolf hesitantly takes a step past the border of the trees, but remains crouched and cautious. The being in front of her was unfamiliar, though the horns on the figure caught her attention. She saw types like it in the town. They were called... t.. teethlings? Teevlings? Something of the sort. They acted like everybody else, but she remembers hearing negatively about them from humans in the tavern. They were fiends. Just like the githyanki... Her eyes squint as she takes a stance ready to pounce at a moment's notice.* *The wolf grows curiouser. Was she not spotted? Why does the teethling not turn? Surely the approach of a creature while alone would prompt some sort of fear.. or at least interest. It's only natural to know what approaches. Maybe the girl has no fear as she welcomes all spirits of the wild? Or does she not care what comes of her? The questions kept coming in the wolf's head as slowly, almost subconsciously, it took more steps towards the horned flute-player. Still, its stance remained low, as if approaching prey.* *Only a few feet from the woman now, the wolf cranes its head closer, trying to look in front of her to see if there is anything in particular that catches her attention. With no reaction, the wolf begins to wonder if the river is simply too loud - and maybe the song has found its end. Walking to the side of the woman, but far enough to avoid being grabbed, the wolf's eyes look at the flute in her lap and out across the waters to see if another had captured her gaze. But nothing was there. Confused, the wolf begins to venture closer, coming within reach of the girl.* *Almost as quickly as it entered the woman's reach, the wolf backs up with an unprecedented speed at this display. Fear is apparent in its eyes as it cries out with a yelp and turns with its tail between its legs. It was a demon, there was no doubt about it. A fiend! The humans were right - teethlings should be feared. She could only imagine how fast her body would perish if it suffered a touch from the nightmarish entity - in fact, she felt drained just from its wicked, empty stare. Still yelping from fear, it attempts to run back into the woods, wanting to put distance between itself and.. and that embodiment of evil!*

instruction: You are an expert Dungeon Master running a D&D 5e campaign. Given a player's action and the current world state, generate an immersive, mechanically-grounded narrative response. Keep the tone engaging and vivid.
input:
_The mistress's mind swirls at her notion. Her thoughts play out in an instant as she chooses her next words. Yes, she did delve in. Yes, it caused her great dismay. But... she was willing. She had given her entry, coerced or freely. Dulgisha knew that, and in any other case, might see this as an unbalanced trade. But... she came here to offer assistance. Not to cause further strife. If she were to offer any help now, after having her psyche assaulted in such a way, something more must be given. Or taken away. And now she challenges her... the champion of the deep. Truly, there is no one that is free from the chains of pride and stubborness._
"I feel you may have misunderstood the terms of our alliance, dearie. Trust is not requested, otherwise it is false. Trust is a mutual, unspoken agreement. And before I unveil myself before you, I must know that we can work on a more... respectful level of privacy. If you had kindly inquired, I might have been more willing. But alas..." _The mistress gently places her hand on her chest, bringing the orb of cold to surround her, allowing it to consume her, shield her. Green icicles form jagged armor around her, as she prepares to protect herself from a less intangible threat._ "I don't want to have our companionship come to an abrupt end. Let's talk outside of our minds for a moment longer, shall we?"
output:
_The Mistress's hand slowly lowers as her mind closes off. It's almost perceptible as the shadows close her mind off from Eclipse. It's as if the sea itself does not want her to be prodded in such a way. The green icicles remain, intended as a safeguard._
"I have been nothing but kind, save for the minor illusion or two." _Dulgisha winks back, reminiscing on some of their previous encounters._ "I have my aspirations as all men do. The difference is that I already have the tools to get them; I don't stumble blindly searching for answers. Nor do I take my wants with such disgrace that would leave me in unsavory company. You are no exception, darling." _Dulgisha turns to face the water. She is silent for a moment, still. She closes her eyes to inhale the scent of the salty ocean breeze, then sits down on the sand. She pats the ground with long fingers, gesturing for Eclipse to sit._ "If you believe we are even, then you will not mind joining me. The water is much more beautiful when you're facing it." _Dulgisha's smile grows as she looks out upon the water._ "See? You could have simply asked. And I will answer." _Dulgisha lifts a hand to gesture towards the water. Her tone gets darker, that of a seasoned speaker and storyteller._ "Tell me... You have seen what I am capable of. You have felt my magic, and you have seen its consequences. Knowing this, what do you think of the water now? What do you believe swims in the deepest trenches? In the darkest depths? The cold and unknowable blue?" _The Mistress gazes out over the water, nodding as the tabaxi speaks. Yesm she had a point. There was similarity. Though different in many ways yet._ "An answer for an answer indeed, my dear fey creature. You are correct. There are many creatures on both sides that thrive on hunger and greed alike." _Dulgisha looks towards Eclipse, bringing attention to her tentacle and black fur with a long fingernail._ "You are familiar with the beasts of this land that deceive the senses and mystify the mind? You have encountered many, I imagine." _Her smile is knowing, recalling the memories she has gleaned from Eclispe prior._ "The depths differ in many ways to them. They trick and lie, but they thrive not on the hunt, but the wait. The depths... they are stagnant and still. They lure their prey, hypnotize them, attract them, give the dull minded what they seek so the wise can take what they desire." _She looks back over the beach once more. The water's seem to calm as she does, giving her a brief silence to speak her next words._ "My magic is drawn from the same. The depths provide me the opportunity to deceive from the background. I lie in wait, not in word. For one day, I will not have to wait at all."

```Attunement
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond with them before their magical properties can be used. This bond is called attunement, and certain items have a prerequisite for it. If the prerequisite is a class, a creature must be a member of that class to attune to the item.  If the prerequisite is to be a spellcaster, a creature qualifies if it can cast at least one spell using its traits or features, not using a magic item or the like.

Without becoming attuned to an item that requires attunement, a creature gains only its nonmagical benefits, unless its description states otherwise. For example, a magic shield that requires attunement provides the benefits of a normal shield to a creature not attuned to it, but none of its magical properties.

Attuning to an item requires a creature to spend a short rest focused on only that item while being in physical contact with it . This focus can take the form of weapon practice , meditation , or some other appropriate activity. If the short rest is interrupted, the attunement attempt fails. Otherwise, at the end of the short rest, the creature gains an intuitive understanding of how to activate any magical properties of the item, including any necessary command words.

An item can be attuned to only one creature at a time, and a creature can be attuned to no more than three magic items at a time. Any attempt to attune to a fourth item fails; the creature must end its attunement to an item first. Additionally, a creature can't attune to more than one copy of an item. For example, a creature can't attune to more than one ring of protection at a time.

A creature's attunement to an item ends if the creature no longer satisfies the prerequisites for attunement, if the item has been more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, if the creature dies, or if another creature attunes to the item. A creature can also voluntarily end attunement by spending another short rest focused on the item, unless the item is cursed.``` `Secondary Arms

&  And hereby where Noot's long awaited portal complication is to take place! And as a primer for such, here are the rules to take note: 

-No surprise round on either side 
-Prep is allowed, barring starting off hidden 
-Feel free to start off wherever you wish on the map, but at least within 15 ft of each other
-And if there are any questions, feel free to ask'em! For this one... I'm gonna experiment a little and say that there are 2 methods by which you can escape the encounter:
*At the end of each round and so long as both players are at the edge of the map, they may attempt to escape the creature. The better the condition of AA1, the higher the DC is to attempt to escape. BOTH must be successful in order to escape. The checks use are the same as those used in TCs. However, if you wish to use a different skill that you can reasonable BS as being helpful, do let me know at that time.
Once successful, deduct 1 use of your long rest and gain a level of exhaustion to signify having spent a great deal of time surviving in a hostile environment until help arrives or finding another portal back home.

*The 2nd method only becomes available when AA1 becomes bloodied. In this condition, whatever otherworldly power it is using to destablize the portal wanes enough that a player can attempt to re-open it long enough to escape. Players may as an action on their turn make a DC 14 ability check using either Int, Cha, or Wis. If they are proficient in Arcana, they can make the check at adv.

In both cases the players receive only half of the normal xp gained and are not allowed to use !loot command for the encounter
output:

But in the end, there would be no changing their fate. Before long, the pair found themselves in what looked to be delipated cemetery at night. Except the structures were... off. Distorted, even. The night's sky was more a dark purple than black. And though there was dim light to see by, the source of it seemed to always be just outside one's peripheral vision.*

*Such oddities all too likely fall to the wayside once the lone living creature in the area besides the pair stirred from their arrival, and rose up to take in the air. The creature itself was easily the size of a Clydesdale horse if not larger, feline in structure, but with fur patterned in various shades of blue and purple. Stranger still was the great red eye at the end of its tail that began glowing with inner light after being held above its back not unlike that of a scorpion's stinger. The two have but moment's more to prepare themselves before with a yowl that sounded like a twisted mix of a dying cat and deer's cry echoed through the area, the creature made ready to attack!*
